source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise & ICS (curated operational subset)

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries probe victim infrastructure with port, vulnerability and service scans to enumerate exploitable entry points.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Host Information
techniques.description: Adversaries collect host details such as OS, firmware, browser and security software to tailor follow-on attacks.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Identity Information
techniques.description: Adversaries collect names, email addresses and credentials to support phishing and credential attacks.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.description: Adversaries send deceptive messages to elicit information or credentials from targeted users.

techniques.name: Gather Victim Network Information
techniques.description: Adversaries map IP ranges, DNS records and network topology before attempting intrusion.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities
techniques.description: Adversaries acquire malware, exploits, certificates or tooling from markets and public sources.

techniques.name: Develop Capabilities
techniques.description: Adversaries build custom malware, exploits or signed certificates for their operations.

techniques.name: Acquire Infrastructure
techniques.description: Adversaries purchase or rent domains, VPS, cloud accounts and botnets to support operations.

techniques.name: Stage Capabilities
techniques.description: Adversaries upload tooling to staging locations and prepare infrastructure before execution.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversaries send malicious emails with attachments or links to gain a foothold.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit internet-facing services such as VPNs, web apps and gateways to enter the network.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries use VPN, RDP, SSH and remote management services to access victim environments.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries reuse legitimate credentials to blend in and move through the environment.

techniques.name: Replication Through Removable Media
techniques.description: Adversaries spread via removable drives, including into air-gapped or OT networks.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.description: Adversaries compromise software, firmware or hardware suppliers to reach downstream victims.

techniques.name: Hardware Additions
techniques.description: Adversaries introduce rogue devices such as implants or wireless access points into a network.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries execute commands through PowerShell, Bash, Python, WMI or similar interpreters.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries rely on users opening malicious files or links to trigger execution.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse WMI for local and remote execution, discovery and persistence.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.description: Adversaries create scheduled tasks, cron jobs or systemd timers to run malicious code.

techniques.name: System Services
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse service execution mechanisms to launch payloads with elevated context.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries configure autostart entries so their code runs at boot or logon.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process
techniques.description: Adversaries install or alter system services and daemons to maintain persistence.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: Adversaries create local, domain or cloud accounts to retain access.

techniques.name: Server Software Component
techniques.description: Adversaries implant web shells or malicious server modules to persist on exposed systems.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries modify accounts, roles, permissions or credentials to escalate and persist.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject code into legitimate processes to evade detection and gain context.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
techniques.description: Adversaries clear logs, delete files and wipe command history to hide activity.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.description: Adversaries disable AV, EDR, firewalls or logging to reduce detection.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries encode, pack or encrypt payloads to hinder analysis.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse signed system binaries such as rundll32 or mshta to run code.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Adversaries alter registry settings for persistence, configuration or defence evasion.

techniques.name: Rootkit
techniques.description: Adversaries use kernel or user-mode rootkits to hide files, processes and network activity.

techniques.name: Pre-OS Boot
techniques.description: Adversaries modify bootloaders, firmware or BIOS to persist below the operating system.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries extract credential material from LSASS, SAM, NTDS or memory.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: Adversaries harvest browser, keychain and password-manager stores.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.description: Adversaries search files, environment variables and repositories for plaintext secrets.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries attempt password guessing, spraying or credential stuffing against accounts.

techniques.name: Modify Authentication Process
techniques.description: Adversaries patch or reconfigure authentication to accept attacker-controlled credentials.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
techniques.description: Adversaries flood users with MFA prompts to obtain approval through fatigue.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate local and domain accounts to identify targets.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries gather host configuration, OS version and patch level.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate reachable hosts through ping sweeps, ARP and directory queries.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries scan for open services and protocols to find further attack paths.

techniques.name: Permission Groups Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate groups and roles to find privileged accounts.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries list running processes to locate security tooling and targets.

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries inspect active network connections to understand topology.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries use RDP, SMB, SSH, WinRM and VNC to move between systems.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries copy tools and payloads to other systems after initial access.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
techniques.description: Adversaries use pass-the-hash, pass-the-ticket or stolen tokens to authenticate.

techniques.name: Remote Service Session Hijacking
techniques.description: Adversaries hijack existing remote sessions to inherit authenticated access.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Adversaries collect files and data from compromised hosts before exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
techniques.description: Adversaries harvest data from SMB shares and network storage.

techniques.name: Email Collection
techniques.description: Adversaries search and export mailbox content for intelligence and credentials.

techniques.name: Input Capture
techniques.description: Adversaries capture keystrokes, screens or clipboard content on victim systems.

techniques.name: Data Staged
techniques.description: Adversaries gather collected data in a staging location before exfiltration.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.description: Adversaries compress and encrypt collected data to simplify exfiltration.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries blend C2 traffic into HTTP, DNS or other common application protocols.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries download additional tools and payloads into the victim network.

techniques.name: Protocol Tunneling
techniques.description: Adversaries encapsulate C2 traffic inside DNS, SSH or other allowed protocols.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.description: Adversaries route traffic through proxies, including compromised internal hosts.

techniques.name: Web Service
techniques.description: Adversaries use legitimate cloud and web services as C2 channels.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt victim data, typically for ransomware extortion.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries delete shadow copies and backups to prevent restoration.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.description: Adversaries stop critical services to disrupt operations during attacks.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.description: Adversaries destroy data and system files to cause irreversible damage.

techniques.name: Network Denial of Service
techniques.description: Adversaries flood networks or services to deny availability.

techniques.name: Data Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries alter stored or transmitted data to mislead or disrupt operations.

techniques.name: Manipulation of Control
techniques.description: ICS adversaries manipulate controller state or setpoints to affect physical processes.

techniques.name: Modify Parameter
techniques.description: ICS adversaries change device parameters such as alarm thresholds or calibration values.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.description: ICS adversaries send unauthorized protocol commands to field devices.

techniques.name: Modify Controller Tasking
techniques.description: ICS adversaries alter PLC program logic or task scheduling.

techniques.name: Activate Firmware Update Mode
techniques.description: ICS adversaries force devices into firmware update mode to disrupt protections.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.description: ICS adversaries exfiltrate engineering documents, historian data and configuration exports.
